citywide_export.rule: the export of a date is fetched before the Status Changes page of that date; a withdrawal or denial dated on or after the export date is the later record, and the file is not counted as pending

reference_files.out_of_order_means: more than 5 higher file numbers carry a date more than 3 days earlier

estimate_rule.rule: median filing date of up to 5 files below and 5 above by number, all within 300 numbers, at least two on each side, agreeing to within 30 days; never later than the file's outcome date
estimate_rule.threshold: used only if test B (all) has median error <= 2.0 days and p90 <= 7.0 days

priority_drawing.rule: never-issued file (withdrawn, denied or pending; no licence record on the file) of type 21, 47 or 48 that is an original: reported action ORI or, with no reported action, no Transfer-From/To on its status records. The filing date plays no part.

evidence_only_application_windows.window_day_means: a day on which 30 or more entries were filed (reported filing dates only)

reading.counts_are: files; a file counts once if any of its licence-type records fits
what_status_changes_can_and_cannot_show: How it works: the report lists a licence-type record on every date on which its status changed, and every listing shows the record's latest transition as of the day the page was fetched, not the change made on the listed date. 90,142 of 91,738 files listed on more than one date show one and the same transition on every date; the rest are files with several licence-type records, each with its own latest transition (345 files have a single licence-type record that reads differently on different dates).

It can show, for an application that was never issued: the filing date (the record's first date) and the withdrawal or denial date (its last date). 12,213 never-issued withdrawn files have a record with exactly two dates, 101.0 days apart at the median (p10 42.0, p90 500.0); their first dates run in file-number order (median error 0.0 days, p90 0.5, N=12,569), as filing dates must.

It can show, for a licence that was issued: the issue date and the date of its latest later change (cancelled, surrendered, revoked ...). Of 38,866 files with a PEND to ACTIVE record on two dates, the first date is the Original Issue Date in 38,079 and is the date of the file's row in Issued Licenses in 38,079 (the second date is, and the first is not, in 3). The second date follows 1.0 day later at the median (p90 3.0): it is the next business day and is not an event in any other report.

It cannot show when an issued application was filed: an issued record carries no date before its Original Issue Date, so days from filing to issue cannot be read from this report. Here 58,159 issued files take a filing date estimated from the file number, 196 take one from a withdrawn licence type on the same file and 4,641 have none.

It cannot show a history: only the latest transition survives. An application withdrawn and later reinstated and issued reads as issued; a licence issued and later cancelled reads ACTIVE to CANCEL. Protests, hearings and conditions are not in it. An application still pending with no status change is not in it at all (it is in New Applications only), and nothing filed before the archive's first day has a filing date.

Denials do appear: 91 files read PEND to DENIED (1 in San Francisco county). The weekly Legal Actions Filed and Finalized reports hold accusations against licensees only; no row is an application denial.

Not applications: PEND to CANCEL (876 files), PEND to NREN (83 files), PEND to SUREND (22 files). Every such record carries an Original Issue Date, so it is a licence that was pending for another reason (a transfer out, for example) and then ended.

workload_partial_years: The archive covers 2019-01-01 to 2026-11-09; a fiscal year it covers only in part is labelled '(partial: first day to last day)' in workload_from_archive and is not compared with ABC

limits: Priority entries. The rule is: never issued, general type (21, 47, 48), original. It does not use the filing date. 156 entries have a reported filing date outside every application window and are counted as entries all the same. A transfer whose status rows carry no Transfer-From/To would be counted as an entry: among issued general-type files with a reported transfer action, 65 of 14,105 carry none. 7 pending general-type files are known from the citywide export alone, with no action and no status record: their class is unknown (shown as original, inferred) and they are not counted as entries.

Withdrawals against ABC. Withdrawn files that are not priority entries come out a few per cent under ABC's Applications Withdrawn in most years. Likely reason, NOT applied: a drawing winner who withdraws later is an ordinary withdrawal to ABC. Priority entries withdrawn 12 or more months after filing, by fiscal year of withdrawal: 2019-20 1, 2020-21 22, 2021-22 37, 2022-23 42, 2023-24 53, 2024-25 59, 2025-26 58. Moving them would need a cut-off chosen against ABC's totals, so they stay priority entries.
FY2021-22 withdrawals stay well under ABC's figure with or without that adjustment. ABC restated that year's figure downward on a later page (abc_licensing_table_cross_check). Unexplained.

Only a record's latest transition survives in Status Changes, so a withdrawal that was later reversed is not counted as one: 241 files now carry a record that reads from WTHDRN or WITHDRAWN to another status. This biases every year's withdrawals slightly low.

Issued files against ABC. With temporary permits (type 30) left out, issued files are a few per cent under ABC's Permanent Licenses Issued in every year, and further under Applications Recommended for Approval. ABC's own issued figure is below its approved figure every year; ABC also counts a licence number once per duplicate number and issue date where a file counts once here. The rest is unexplained.

Original and transfer investigations. ABC's pages do not say which actions go in which table. The grouping used (premises transfers with originals) comes from the second verifier's regression of ABC's per-office approved counts on action classes over 152 office-years (original table: ORI 1.02, PRM 0.96, PER -0.04; transfer table: PER 1.05, FID/DPR/STK 0.96); it is not recomputed here. ICO is placed with originals on thin evidence; MBR, MBM, STM, EXC-only and blank actions are placed with transfers and are too rare to test. Transfer investigations stay under ABC's after regrouping: an approved transfer with no issue in the year is not visible in the reports.

Offices. The district code on a file is the office that holds the premises today. FY2019-20 San Francisco office rows carry a territory note (sf_office_territory); no per-office figure is adjusted, and the handover date of San Mateo county is inferred, not stated by ABC. The same effect may explain other office-years (LA / Metro in FY2019-20); not tested.
ABC's workload pages define none of the Licensing summary rows in words. What a row counts is inferred from table titles and from arithmetic between the tables.

Filing dates. Status Changes never shows when an issued application was filed; the filing date of an issued file is estimated from its file number and labelled so. Nothing filed before the archive's first day has a filing date.

Pending. A file is pending if New Applications lists it today or the citywide export shows it pending. The export is San Francisco only and a day older than the Status Changes page of the same date; a withdrawal or denial dated on or after the export date overrides it (citywide_export).

Business names. An individual licensee is recognised by ABC's 'SURNAME, GIVEN' form with no entity suffix; for those files no name is published, DBA included. A company's DBA can itself be a person's name (an eponymous restaurant or winery); it is the trade name of a company and is published.

Part-years. The archive covers 2019-01-01 to 2026-11-09; a fiscal year it covers only in part is labelled '(partial: first day to last day)' in workload_from_archive and is not compared with ABC. Calendar-year tables carry a partial_year note.
